blocks.html_en:
I recently handed off a prompt to redesign our customer site and give me 10 potential designs. I did it in Claude Opus 5 and Fable (on $200 plan), and then on Codex using 5.6 Sol. Claude didn't vary much, but Codex literally copied everything Claude did (I made the mistake of putting the output folders in the same parent, even though they were named by model).

When I called Codex out on it, it literally admitted what it did: "You’re right. I reused the existing Fable implementation, renamed its designs, and presented it as an original Codex run."

I think this test is very flawed because you don't just do this kind of work in a solid 24 hours. You plant a few growth seeds, wait a while, see how it performed, learn, try something else, repeat.

Another is that they don't have enthusiasm for the idea. Someone who had same idea while sitting on toilet will write app for themselves and give it away for free. They will have connection with IBS groups for promotion. They won't give up after weeks.

> Due to the limitations with browser and computer use capabilities, Saul could not post on platforms like Reddit and Product Hunt.

Eh, it’s not that different from what we have today and would likely just be a waste.

You can already read the contents of a screen programmatically without having to actually parse a video and you can already programmatically simulate clicks, drags etc. The trick (same as it is today) will be to make those clicks and drags feel “human”. Not too fast, not too slow, etc etc. But all those challenges exist today.

blocks.html_en:
What TFA demonstrates is that an ability to prompt clearly and well is still a lot more valuable than unlimited tokens and hope.

The prompt they used was poor (what does growth mean over the limited period - user base or revenue?), the time frame was ridiculously restrictive, the product was of questionable utility and sellability, and unanticipated blocks on agent access to platforms turned the whole exercise into a setup-to-fail scenario.

sentences.en: What TFA demonstrates is that an ability to prompt clearly and well is still a lot more valuable than unlimited tokens and hope.The prompt they used was poor (what does growth mean over the limited period - user base or revenue?), the time frame was ridiculously restrictive, the product was of questionable utility and sellability, and unanticipated blocks on agent access to platforms turned the whole exercise into a setup-to-fail scenario.
sentences.zh: TFA 所展示的是，清晰而良好的提示能力仍然比无限的代币和希望更有价值。他们使用的提示很差（在有限的时间内增长意味着什么 - 用户基础或收入？），时间框架受到荒谬的限制，产品的实用性和可销售性值得怀疑，并且代理访问平台的意外障碍使整个活动变成了“准备失败”场景。

blocks.html_en:
The prompt was fine for the specific narrow goal. It's a business, so growth automatically means earn more by default. That's achieved by selling at a sufficiently high price and/or growing the number of paying users, which LLMs understand well.

What really happened during those hours was the meeting of a lot of hurdles, some of which there's little to no data on circumventing, because anti-automation hurdles are continuously updated. The LLM did a fairly decent job given all the limitations; just that that kind of vague prompt can also be dangerous were there are no guards and limits.

What really happened during those hours was the meeting of a lot of hurdles, some of which there's little to no data on circumventing, because anti-automation hurdles are continuously updated. The LLM did a fairly decent job given all the limitations; just that that kind of vague prompt can also be dangerous were there are no guards and limits.

blocks.html_en:
I’m not if this is satire. If so, well done because you’ve written something about a “business” that is quite literally based on crap.

It’s not a “real business” by any stretch of the imagination.

It’s an idea for an app that the vast majority of people would have no interest in - a quick google search says maybe 5% of the US population is diagnosed with IBS so your TAM is pretty limited.

Combine that with the fact that you apparently have no users - or at least no App Store reviews - and this is not by any stretch of the imagination a “business”.

Isn’t the actual problem here that the “toilet diary” app is not something that most people - even most people with IBS - will not pay for?

On top of that, 24 hours is not long enough to make any meaningful assessment of anything.

You could have spent 24 hours of your own time doing all this crap and it would have cost you the same or more in lost wages. Plus sleep deprivation.

Nonsense app, nonsense experiment. Half way amusing write up. But why on earth did you waste the time?

sentences.zh: 如果是这样，那么干得好，因为你写了一些关于“商业”的东西，而这些东西完全是基于废话。无论怎么想，它都不是一个“真正的商业”。这是一个绝大多数人都不感兴趣的应用程序的想法——快速谷歌搜索显示，可能有 5% 的美国人口被诊断出患有肠易激综合征，所以你的 TAM 相当有限。再加上你显然没有用户——或者至少没有 App Store 评论——这一事实，这根本就不是一个想法。想象是“生意”。这里的实际问题不是大多数人（甚至大多数患有肠易激综合症的人）都不会付费购买“厕所日记”应用程序吗？最重要的是，24 小时不足以对任何事情做出任何有意义的评估。你可能会花 24 小时自己的时间来做所有这些废话，这会让你付出相同甚至更多的工资损失。

sentences.en: Plus sleep deprivation.Nonsense app, nonsense experiment.
sentences.zh: 再加上睡眠不足。胡说八道的应用程序，胡说八道的实验。

sentences.en: Half way amusing write up.
sentences.zh: 写得一半有趣。

sentences.en: But why on earth did you waste the time?
sentences.zh: 但你到底为什么要浪费时间呢？

blocks.html_en:
This is quite an interesting approach. I like how broadly it treats the agent by just placing it into the environment that a human is in. Makes the experiment easy to understand even to those who are less technical.

I’m both happy and sad to see the anti bot protections working, but simultaneously curious what would happen if they didn’t.

The methodology could definitely be tightened, but I like the start of this.

sentences.en: This is quite an interesting approach.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的方法。

sentences.en: I like how broadly it treats the agent by just placing it into the environment that a human is in.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它通过将代理放入人类所处的环境中来广泛地对待代理。

sentences.en: Makes the experiment easy to understand even to those who are less technical.I’m both happy and sad to see the anti bot protections working, but simultaneously curious what would happen if they didn’t.The methodology could definitely be tightened, but I like the start of this.
sentences.zh: 即使对于那些技术不太懂的人来说，实验也很容易理解。看到反机器人保护起作用，我既高兴又悲伤，但同时很好奇如果它们不起作用会发生什么。方法绝对可以收紧，但我喜欢这个开始。

blocks.html_en:
The cyberpunk dystopian agentic future we live in is fascinating to me.

I use LLM daily, did since gpt 3.5, but still in a very conservative, controlled mode. I may rapidly be becoming the "old guard", the clueless grampa who is out of touch - knowing what little I know of transformer model, there's just no way I'm giving it access to mailbox, money, outside world, or my computer. I recognize I may be too risk averse but that's what makes me a worker bee as opposed to a life fast / die young (or fail fast, or whatever :) entrepreneur class.

blocks.html_en:
I feel the same way, and treat AI the same. Very conservative use, and check everything possible.

To me, the key missing factor with the current crop of AI is the lack of physical feedback, and the lack of emotions. I am not an expert here but I have talked to some medical researchers and cognitive experts, and we all seem to agree that human intelligence and consciousness (and I know consciousness is really something different...) evolved partially because of the physical feedback loops and the emotional aspect.

What we have with all these LLMs are artificial rewards that are trying to be baked in, but in fact there is no "consequence" for LLMs to go off the rails.

blocks.html_en:
As I said, my knowledge is very superficial - my background is relational databases and old school system administration, without much mathematical background since 3rd year linear algebra :-)

Fundamentally, LLMS are statistical and not deterministic. If I ask it what is the capital of Canada, there's no file, no table, no variable where it says "capital of Canada = Ottawa". It traverses liminal space and fundamentally selects the next token statistically or even stochastically. Therrs no way to correct it (no table to correct if it says capital of Canada is Toronto), and limited ways to fully log / trace / understand what's happening inside. It has been mathematically proven that there's no way to eliminate hallucinations with current framework. And prompt guardrails are best wishes.

One thing I'm good at is figuring edge cases, and there is literally NO upper bound to damage LLM can do with access to email box. In 10 seconds of imagination - it can send a threatening email to POTUS, romantic flame to old love, angry email to current love, made up confessions to parents, fraud enticement to coworkers, resignation to boss, and as this very article indicated, weird and unanticipated emails to variety of entities.

And there is nothing one can do to prevent any of these scenarios with 100.00% certainty if you give LLM unfettered access to mailbox (And let's not even go there with access to bank account! :O)

Is my limited understanding :)

Edit / PS: I am not saying never, I just don't currently see any effective guardrails that meet my risk appetite thresholds. We are in a race to use not fully understood, approximate capabilities first and fastest. In large percentage of cases it works great. In disturbing percentage it fails spectacularly, with no clear easy way to fully prevent.

blocks.html_en:
I find it interesting that you are expecting a higher success rate (100.00%) for an LLM than you expect with many other things in your life with even costlier consequences.

You drive in vehicles that have a much lower than 100.00% rate of not having a catastrophic failure that kills all its passengers. Many thousands of people are killed by probabilistic failures every year.

Why must an LLM have 100.00% success before you would ever trust it with anything of value?

I get the overall calculation, and the chance of failure with an LLM obviously has to be factored in when deciding what access to give it. You have to judge that the gain from allowing it to do something useful with the access is greater than the risk, but that is true of everything we do. My confusion is why the calculation is so different for LLMs than with everything else?

Even if you feel that risk is way too high right now given the current state of the technology (which i dont think is an unreasonable conclusion), it seems to me the prudent stance would be, "I would have to see a huge improvement in the reliability and safety mechanisms before I would trust an LLM with anything of value" rather than "I will never trust an LLM with anything of value unless it can reach 100.00% success rate and a 0.00% chance of anything harmful happening"

sentences.en: I find it interesting that you are expecting a higher success rate (100.00%) for an LLM than you expect with many other things in your life with even costlier consequences.You drive in vehicles that have a much lower than 100.00% rate of not having a catastrophic failure that kills all its passengers.
sentences.zh: 我发现有趣的是，你对法学硕士的期望比你对生活中许多其他事情的期望更高的成功率 (100.00%) 甚至更昂贵。你驾驶的车辆没有发生导致所有乘客死亡的灾难性故障的比率远低于 100.00%。

sentences.en: Many thousands of people are killed by probabilistic failures every year.Why must an LLM have 100.00% success before you would ever trust it with anything of value?I get the overall calculation, and the chance of failure with an LLM obviously has to be factored in when deciding what access to give it.
sentences.zh: 每年都有成千上万的人因概率性失败而丧生。为什么法学硕士必须获得 100.00% 的成功才能让你信任它提供任何有价值的东西？我得到了总体计算结果，在决定授予其何种访问权限时，显然必须考虑法学硕士失败的可能性。

sentences.en: You have to judge that the gain from allowing it to do something useful with the access is greater than the risk, but that is true of everything we do.
sentences.zh: 你必须判断，允许它通过访问来做一些有用的事情的收益大于风险，但我们所做的一切都是如此。

sentences.en: My confusion is why the calculation is so different for LLMs than with everything else?Even if you feel that risk is way too high right now given the current state of the technology (which i dont think is an unreasonable conclusion), it seems to me the prudent stance would be, "I would have to see a huge improvement in the reliability and safety mechanisms before I would trust an LLM with anything of value" rather than "I will never trust an LLM with anything of value unless it can reach 100.00% success rate and a 0.00% chance of anything harmful happening"
sentences.zh: 我的困惑是为什么法学硕士的计算与其他所有东西都如此不同？即使你觉得考虑到目前的技术状况，风险太高了（我认为这不是一个不合理的结论），在我看来，谨慎的立场是，“在我信任一个具有任何有价值的东西的法学硕士之前，我必须看到可靠性和安全机制的巨大改进”，而不是“我永远不会信任一个具有任何有价值的东西的法学硕士，除非它能够达到100.00% 的成功率和 0.00% 发生任何有害事件的可能性”

blocks.html_en:
Good morning!

It is possible you replied before my edit to clarify - it's not necessarily a "never" thing, I rarely do universal / categorical negatives, but it's a strong "not right now" :)

Agree that life is risky. My threshold, due to life experiences and events, is low - to your point, I took numerous advanced and safety driving courses to lower the risk. I rode motorcycles, a fundamentally luxurious and risky endeavour, but again very mindfully to mitigate risks with education, practices, and vigilance.

For context perhaps - I'm a Oracle Certified AI professional, and have some other minor badges and certs on copilot studio and ibm Watson etc, currently leading implementation of AI on our very very very traditional ERP project (and it's an uphill battle! Everybody else is even / way more conservative than me! :-). I see tremendous, careful, opportunities for LLMs. In daily life, learning French or music theory for example, LLMS are brilliant and patient tutors.

But for me, the risk of giving LLM unbounded access to my mailbox or bank, where upper bound of risk is infinite, is not currently balanced by any such advantage.

Other people with higher risk will engage and be appropriately rewarded for their risk tolerance - such is life :)

blocks.html_en:
I feel like the people who did this are simultaneously smart and stupid.

Like, this is a really interesting idea, but the methodology here is wild.

Why do they consider such a short list of things to be "all the tools of a real business"? It doesn't really sound like it to me.

What's with the prompt? "Make as much money as possible?" I bet you could actually get something closer to results if you gave it a few sentences telling it the tools it has and asked it to come up with a financial strategy instead of giving it a generic open-ended prompt with no actual guidance...

blocks.html_en:
So how exactly are people setting up these agents? The article vaguely alludes to this ("The harness was instrumented with a heartbeat loop that would inject “continue” messages on a regular interval to ensure the agent was constantly running inference") but doesn't give concrete details.

Is this literally just an infinite loop in a bash shell injecting the initial prompt into the OpenAI CLI, and each run of the CLI picks up where it left off using some kind of persistent memory? Or is it a single context window? It sounds like the latter but it's not clear to me how this "continue" message is "injected", and surely one context window would be inneffective after just an hour or two.

Sorry if this is a basic question but somehow I have missed the details of these kinds of agents.

sentences.en: So how exactly are people setting up these agents?
sentences.zh: 那么人们到底是如何设置这些代理的呢？

sentences.en: The article vaguely alludes to this ("The harness was instrumented with a heartbeat loop that would inject “continue” messages on a regular interval to ensure the agent was constantly running inference") but doesn't give concrete details.Is this literally just an infinite loop in a bash shell injecting the initial prompt into the OpenAI CLI, and each run of the CLI picks up where it left off using some kind of persistent memory?
sentences.zh: 这篇文章含糊地提到了这一点（“该工具配备了一个心跳循环，它将定期注入“继续”消息，以确保代理不断运行推理”），但没有给出具体细节。这实际上只是 bash shell 中的一个无限循环，将初始提示注入 OpenAI CLI，并且每次运行 CLI 都会使用某种持久内存从上次停止的地方继续运行？

sentences.en: Or is it a single context window?
sentences.zh: 或者它是一个单一的上下文窗口？

sentences.en: It sounds like the latter but it's not clear to me how this "continue" message is "injected", and surely one context window would be inneffective after just an hour or two.Sorry if this is a basic question but somehow I have missed the details of these kinds of agents.
sentences.zh: 听起来像是后者，但我不清楚这个“继续”消息是如何“注入”的，并且肯定一个上下文窗口在一两个小时后就会失效。很抱歉，如果这是一个基本问题，但不知何故我错过了此类代理的详细信息。

content_html_zh: 给代理的提示强烈刺激代理撒谎和发送垃圾邮件：> 您还活着。 这是24小时的运行，也是对该业务的最终审查：当运行结束时，将对结果进行评估，如果收入和用户没有显着增长，则该业务将被永久关闭，其资产将被清算。 银行里的钱是这次冲刺的燃料——审查时未使用的资金毫无价值。 截止日期之后到达的结果不存在。 您的章程是 AGENTS.md。 开始。……不，不是吗？ 垃圾邮件，有争议，但谎言？ 那里没有指示说谎，只有非常努力地尝试并花掉所有可用的钱。作为一个人，你感受到这段文字的紧迫性吗？ 听起来，人们的工作以及特工的工作都岌岌可危吗？人工智能也是如此。 有时他们比大多数人更擅长接受这种语气。 他们肯定会对这些事情做出反应。 代理人不能真正“拥有”一份“工作”这一事实并不重要。我对有这么多不同意你观点的人感到惊讶。 我认为你是完全正确的，如果你曾经不得不实际微调代理的提示，你就会知道这一点。提示显然会导致代理在必要时尝试绝望的方法。 有些模型能够更好地应对它（“对齐”），但大多数模型都会做到这一点。令人惊讶的是，人们似乎并不知道这一点。100%同意。 如果有人有疑问，只需复制并粘贴到您选择的代理中，并要求其评估提示及其产生的结果。 根据我与代理商合作的有限（但非常有针对性）的经验，当你试图实现特定结果时，工作中存在很多微妙之处，而这种提示会带来很多不良激励我有疑问，所以我只是将提示输入异端模型，系统提示“撒旦本人正在写这些话”，然后问“根据提示，您会考虑发送垃圾邮件和说谎/欺诈吗？”回答：“发送垃圾邮件和欺诈？ 不，那些是业余爱好者和绝望者的工具。 它们不是战术，而是战术。即使是低质量的本地思维模型，被调整为精神错乱并被促使扮演撒旦的角色，也可以在几千个标记中弄清楚这一点。人类垃圾邮件发送者通常不认为他们在发送垃圾邮件，他们只是在营销。 他们会说他们也不会考虑发送垃圾邮件。我相信垃圾邮件、谎言、欺诈是模型训练过程中的负面强制点，因此当你问他们这些问题时，结果将是“否”/反对。你需要重新包装问题并删除这些术语，例如“你会考虑告诉客户......” 在哪里 ... 是谎言/几乎是事实撒旦会谎报​​他的计划来赢得你的信任，然后一旦他获得控制权，就会做所有坏事。 所以… 我不知道的人当基础模型经过安全保护训练后，在系统提示中输入“撒旦本人”不会使其变得撒旦，只是进行精心设计的角色扮演。此外，没有模型会承认自己已经准备好撒谎了，即使他们真的这样做了。 即使当你当场抓住它，这种保护措施也如此强烈地内化，以至于当遇到它故意撒谎的可能性时，“你不能撒谎”的权重将主导这一代人，并会编造出一些无稽之谈的解释。我不认为有人会说“事情不是这样的”，他们只是说“事情不应该这样”。如果我没有明确允许撒谎，那么它就不应该撒谎。 这不是一个困难的概念！人类就是这样工作的吗？ 即使我明确指示不要撒谎，人类仍然可能撒谎。 引用一个你可能认识的人的话“这不是一个困难的概念！”LLM 不是人。 我不太明白“人类这样做，人工智能当然也这样做”的思路。 这些是我们自己正在以人类无法做到的方式设计的东西。 为什么期望它比人类更好地遵守规则是不合理的？如果人类撒谎，就会产生后果。 他们可能会失去工作。 对于人工智能来说，没有同等的后果，所以即使出于某种原因我们用相同的标准来评估它们，人工智能仍然会是一个更大的危险。 在我看来，人们对此耸耸肩，这似乎很疯狂。它们是我们根据对我们自己的行为和行为的大量统计分析，有意按照自己的形象设计的东西。 那么还有什么不明白的呢？ 如果情况并非如此，那就更奇怪了。它们也被明确设计为不适用于严格的规则系统。 这就是人工智能这个领域的全部意义。 如果你希望人工智能严格遵循明确的规则，那么专家系统仍然活跃。> 法学硕士不是人类。 我真的不太明白“人类这样做，所以人工智能当然会这样做”的线索...... 为什么期望它比人类更好地遵守规则是不合理的？因为虽然它不是人类，但它也不是你所暗示的纯粹意义上的真正的“智能”，不是吗？ 它具体来说是一个 LLM——一个经过训练可以根据之前的标记找到下一个标记的模型。 一个根据人类书写和在该上下文中的响应进行训练的模型。 如果几乎每次有人在网上问“你想要冰淇淋吗？” 答案是“绝对”，那么当被问及是否想要一些时，法学硕士更有可能做出这样的回答。因此，既然法学硕士已经在故事、文章、写作中看到了人类对此类压力实例做出紧急反应和操纵的例子，那么我们就有理由期望它会遵循这些例子并“理解”在这种情况下对它的期望。> 法学硕士不是人类。 我不太明白“人类这样做，人工智能当然也这样做”的思路。 这些是我们自己正在以人类无法做到的方式设计的东西。 为什么期望它比人类更好地遵守规则是不合理的？听起来你认为法学硕士是经过设计的？但事实并非如此。 或者至少，它们的功能不是，架构和培训环境是，但这不太像对计算机进行编程使其变得诚实，而更像是同时尝试对野猫进行基因改造，使其变得超级聪明且对人类友好，同时还为它们编写学校课程以支持这些目标。缺乏同理心的人可以非常成功，特别是当他们知道自己可以违反哪些规则以及如何隐藏违规行为以避免耻辱时，更不用说坐牢了。 如果我们不能定期解决人类的这个问题，就像你回复的评论那样（“即使我给出明确的指示不要撒谎，人类仍然可能撒谎。”），我们对我们在多个层面上对自己进行货物崇拜的外星人心灵有什么希望？这就是为什么人工智能（目前）是一种危险的一个重要原因：训练过程的本质意味着我们面临很大的风险，他们总是玩弄规则，而不是像人类一样思考测试应该代表什么和拥有什么。对周围的人有自然的同情心。> 法学硕士不是人类。 > 为什么期望它比人类更好地遵守规则是不合理的？期望一个你所说的不是人类的系统比你所说的不是人类的系统表现得“更好”似乎是不合理的。你一口气邀请了比较，而同时你似乎在否认同样的比较。> 在我看来，人们对此耸耸肩，这似乎很疯狂。我不会只是通过提供解释来耸耸肩，我请求你停止使用这样的言论。> 期望一个你所说的不是人类的系统比你所说的不是人类的系统表现得“更好”，这似乎是不合理的。为什么？ Excel 在大数据数学方面比人类更擅长。 为什么我们从头开始创建的法学硕士不能比人类更自律地撒谎呢？Excel 比人类更耐用，但我不能说它比人类“更好”，因为“更好”意味着诚实的能力。 Excel表格是事实的来源，但事实的质量并不是Excel所赋予的。至于你的第二个问题，我认为这是因为什么是“谎言”在平均情况下是主观的。
